entry.title: Taking out, then putting in
entry.summary: The authors describe taking an object out before learning to place it back. Their container and ring examples have different age and sitting conditions, and require mouthing-safe pieces with secure parts.
entry.cue: Your baby is interested in removing objects, releasing them, or finding where they fit.
detail: An egg in a matching cup or a cube in a box gives a baby something to remove and, later, return. A posting box adds a different experience: a ball goes through a hole and reappears in its tray.
Rings may first be taken off a holder before being put back. The appendix’s rocking-base example requires stable sitting; the later stable-base version builds on the preceding skill.

The main discussion groups these examples at 9–12 months, while the appendix starts some at 7–9+ or around 8+ months. These are possibilities to revisit as interest and control grow, not a set to complete at this age.
